Convention used: a conclusion 'definitely follows' only if it is true in every Venn diagram that fits the statements; 'Some' means at least one; a statement without 'Some' does not by itself guarantee that a group has any member.
questions.shortcut: Some + No gives Some-not.

questions.questionText:
Statements: Some poles are seats. All poles are trees. No coins are trees.
Conclusions:
I. No poles are seats.
II. Some trees are seats.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation:
I. No poles are seats does not follow: in a diagram where only this region is occupied: an item that belongs to seats and poles and trees, not to coins, the statements hold but this fails.
II. Some trees are seats follows: it holds in every diagram that fits the statements (checked region by region).
So only conclusion II holds.
Convention used: a conclusion 'definitely follows' only if it is true in every Venn diagram that fits the statements; 'Some' means at least one; a statement without 'Some' does not by itself guarantee that a group has any member.
questions.shortcut: Quick rules: All+All=All; All+No=No; Some+All=Some; Some+No=Some-not; Some+Some and No+No give nothing; All+Some gives nothing.
